 This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, praying to (a) Call for records in MVC No. 1391/2012 on the file of Principal Senior Civil Judge & A.C.J.M and M.A.C.T. at Puttur (b) Set aside the Judgment and Award dated 01.06.2015 passed by the Principal Senior Civil Judge & A.C.J.M. and M.A.C.T. at Puttur, in MVC No.1391/2012 and enhance the compensation from `5,02,400/- to `10,00,000/- as claimed by the Petitioner in the claim petition.
c) Grant such other and further relief's as this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case in the interest of justice and equity.

This Miscellaneous First Appeal coming on for Final Hearing through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, this day,
the Court delivered the following:
 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Court of the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate and Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal, at Puttur, (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the Tribunal"), in its judgment and award dated 01-06-2015, in M.V.C.No.1391/2012.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The summary of the case of the claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 22-09-2011, at about 9:00 a.m., while he was traveling as a pillion rider on a Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-21/K-6248, being ridden by one Sri. Santhosh, i.e. the first respondent herein and was going on Mangalore-Bangalore NH-75, and approached a place called Nellyadi, Santhekatte, near Post Office of Nellyadi village, Puttur Taluk, due to the rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle by its rider, it dashed against a pedestrian, i.e. a boy and lost his control and the Motor cycle was capsized,
resulting in the road traffic accident in question.

In the said road traffic accident, he (claimant)

2 sustained multiple grievous injuries on his head, face, forehead, right shoulder, right knee and all over the body.

He was shifted to the A.J. Hospital and Research Centre, Mangalore, for treatment,
wherein he was treated as an in-patient, by several specialist Doctors.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The claimant stated that towards medical expenses, he has spent not less than a sum of `2,00,000/-
and expected to spend another sum of `50,000/- towards future medical expenses and spent a sum of `50,000/- towards traveling, food and for other incidental expenses.

He further stated that at the time of occurrence of the road traffic accident, he was working as a Mechanic at Hero Honda Service Station, Nellyadi, Puttur Taluk, and earning monthly income of a sum of `9,000/- per month.

However, due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident and the disability suffered by him,
he could not continue his job.

With this, he has claimed a compensation of a sum of `10,00,000/-,
holding respectively the respondents No.1, 2 and 3, as the driver, owner and insurer of the alleged offending Motor Cycle, liable to pay the compensation to him.

3. Upon service of summons upon the respondents before the Tribunal, all three respondents appeared through their respective counsels and it was respondent No.3 Insurance Company alone which chose to file its statement of objections.
In its Statements of Objections, the Insurer denied all the petition averments including the alleged road traffic accident occurring in the manner as contended by the claimant.
It also denied the nature of the injuries said to have been suffered by the claimant.
Denying the age, income and occupation of the claimant and his alleged disability, the respondent No.3 Insurance Company prayed for rejection of the claim petition.
4. Before the Tribunal, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1 and also examined four more witnesses, as PW-2 to PW-5 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-48 and also Exs.C-1, C-2 and C-3.

On behalf of the respondents, no witness was examined, however, only one document in the form of a copy of the Insurance Policy was got marked as Ex.R-1.
5.

After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:

3 6.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `5,02,400/- with interest at the rate of `6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation, holding the respondents 1 to 3 jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation and directed the Respondent No.3 - Insurer to deposit the award amount.
It is against the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal, seeking enhancement of compensation.
7. While filing this appeal, there was a delay of 472 days.

Thus, on an application - I.A.No.1/2017 filed by the learned counsel for appellant, this Court, on the date 13-03-2018, has condoned the delay of 472 days in filing the appeal, denying the interest on the enhanced compensation, if any, for the said delayed period.
8. Records were called for from the Tribunal and the same are placed before the Court.
9. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) and the learned counsel for respondent No.3 (insurer) before this Court are physically appearing before the Court.
Though notice was served upon the respondents No.1 and 2, they have remained un-represented.
10. Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the materials placed before this Court including the memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the Tribunal records.

11. The present appeal being the claimant's appeal and the respondent Insurer having not preferred either cross-objection or a counter appeal, the question of occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place as alleged by the claimant and also the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is not in dispute.

Further, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1, who, in his examination-in-chief, in the form of Affidavit evidence, has reiterated the contentions taken up by him in his claim petition about the occurrence of the road traffic accident.

He also got produced documents from Exs.P-1 to P-48,
which inter alia includes the copies of the complaint, FIR, scene of offence panchanama, sketch,
Wound Certificate, Disability Certificate and Discharge Summary.
These documents corroborate the evidence of PW-1 about the occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place and in the manner as contended by him in his claim petition.
The evidence of PW-1 that he sustained injuries in the road traffic accident is corroborated with the Wound Certificate at Ex.P-6.

The same is further corroborated by the evidence of Dr. Sunil Shetty (PW-2), Dr. Ullas Shetty (PW-3) and Dr.
Dinesh Kadam (PW-4) respectively.

Therefore, the occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place and in the manner as contended by the claimant in his claim petition and the claimant sustaining multiple grievous injuries in the said road traffic accident stands established.

Hence, respondents 1, 2 and 3, being the driver, owner and insurer of the offending Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-21/K-6248 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to Ravichandra S vs Santhosh on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197754231/
4 the claimant.
Thus, the only question that remains for consideration is about the quantification of the compensation, which, according to the claimant/appellant, is inadequate.

12. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) in his argument submitted that, the injuries and their - 10 - nature would go to show that, the claimant had sustained multiple simple and grievous injuries and he was also treated as an in-patient for a long time in the Hospital, as such, the quantum of compensation awarded towards injury, pain and sufferings is meager and deserves to be enhanced.

He further submitted that the income of the claimant which he has stated at `9,000/- per month is further corroborated by the evidence of his employer who was examined as PW-5 and the Salary Certificate produced and marked by the claimant at Ex.P-8.

Since there being no reasons to disbelieve the same, the Tribunal ought to have considered the income of the claimant at `9,000/-
per month.

Further, stating that the compensation awarded under the other heads is also meager,
the learned counsel for the appellant prayed to allow this appeal.

13. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 - Insurance Company, in his argument submitted that, considering the fact that the claimant has sustained - 11 - multiple grievous injuries, the Tribunal has awarded a reasonable and just compensation of a sum of `75,000/- towards pain and sufferings, as such, the same does not warrant any modification by this Court.

He also submitted that the compensation awarded under the other heads is also in no way less than the actuals and reasonable, as such, they also do not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.
He further submitted that, the income of the claimant, though is claimed to be a sum of `9,000/- per month, however, the same has not been established by him.

Even though PW-5 (alleged employer of the claimant) has been examined as the author of the salary certificate at Ex.P-8, admittedly, the said witness has not produced any salary register extract or other documents, as such, the notional income prevailing for the relevant year is required to be taken.

However, he submitted that, though the Tribunal has taken the notional income as at `6,000/- per month, the same since being short by a sum of `500/-, the same deserves to be enhanced by a sum of `500/- and the notional income is to - 12 - be taken at `6,500/- per month.
With this, he submitted that the appeal does not deserve to be allowed as prayed for by the claimant.

The claimant, as PW-1, has stated that, in the road traffic accident, he sustained multiple grievous injuries.
In his support, he has produced Wound Certificate at Ex.P-6, Discharge Summary at Ex.P-10 and also got examined three Medical Doctors from PW-2 to PW-4.
PW-2 is a Neuro Surgeon who has spoken about he examining the claimant and noticing the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
PW-3 Dr. Ullas Shetty, as a Medico Legal Consultant and working at the A.J. Hospital and Research Centre, Mangalore has stated about the claimant being treated in their Hospital as an in- patient.

- 13 - PW-4 Dr. Dinesh Kadam, a Plastic Surgeon and working at the A.J. Hospital and Research Centre,
Mangalore,

The opinion of all these three Medical Doctors, i.e. PW-2,
PW-3, and PW-4 corroborates the injuries described in the Wound Certificate and mentioned in the Discharge Summary at Ex.P-10.

Accordingly, the claimant is established to have sustained the following injuries:
(i) Lacerated wound measuring 5 cm X 1 cm X bone deep, horizontally, over middle of the forehead (ii) Abrasion, measuring 1 cm X 1 cm. over right shoulder (iii) Abrasion measuring 2 cm X 0.5 cm. over outer aspect of right knee.

(iv) CT Scan of Brain and Face No.24756 shows:
a) Depressed comminuted fracture of frontal bone b) Fracture of nasal bones c) Fracture of cribriform plate of ethmoidal bone d) Fracture of sphenoid on left side e) Fracture of temporal bone on left side f) Fracture of bilateral maxilla g) Fracture of nasal septum - 14 - Ravichandra S vs Santhosh on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197754231/
6 h) Fracture of left orbit i) Extradural haematoma in bilateral frontal and temporal convexity j) Hemorrhagic contusions in bilateral frontal lobe.
The Discharge Summary at Ex.P-10 issued by the A.J. Hospital and Research Centre, Mangalore,
shows that, the claimant was admitted as an in-patient in their Hospital on the date 22-09-2011.
The Wound Certificate at Ex.P-6 issued by the same Hospital would go to show that, he was discharged on the date 04-10-2011.
Thus, for about 12 days, he was treated as an in-patient in the Hospital.

Hence, considering the multiple grievous injuries and also the simple injuries which are large in number, though the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `75,000/- under the said head, I am of the view that the same deserves to be enhanced by a sum of `20,000/-, making it a reasonable amount of a sum of `95,000/- under the said head.
15. The medical expenses incurred by the claimant is corroborated by the medical bills from Exs.P-11 to - 15 - P-43, twenty three medical prescriptions at Ex.P-44, the case sheet at Ex.C-1.

It is considering these aspects, since the Tribunal has arrived at the actual amount of a sum of `2,00,000/- as the expenses incurred by the claimant and held the same towards medical expenses, the same does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.

16. It is after considering that the claimant was in- patient in the Hospital for a period of twelve days, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `10,000/- towards conveyance and other incidental charges.
For no reasons, the said amount can be considered as a lower amount.
Hence, it deserves no modification.
17. Towards food, nutrition and nourishment, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `5,000/-.

Considering the nature of the multiple grievous injuries sustained by the claimant, for which special diet and nourishing food might have been prescribed for him and also the requirement of - 16 - the assistant to attend him during his stay in the Hospital, I am of the view that the compensation of a sum of `5,000/- awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced by a sum of `10,000/-, thus making it in total a sum of `15,000/-.
18. The claimant has contended that at the time of the road traffic accident, he was working as a Mechanic in Hero Honda Motor Bike Service Centre and was getting salary of `9,000/- per month.

sentences.text: In that regard, he got produced a document, calling it as a salary certificate, which is marked as Ex.P-8 and examined one Sri. Naresh, as PW-5, who is said to be the author of the said document.

7

The said witness (PW-5), in his evidence has stated that, for the past several years, he has been running a Motor Cycle Care and Service Centre in the name and style of 'Keerthi Bike Care' at Nellyadi, in which he has been utilising the services of four Mechanics including the present claimant.

He has stated that the present claimant was an experienced Mechanic, as such,
- 17 - he was giving him a salary of `9,000/- per month.
He has stated that till the date of the occurrence of the road traffic accident, the claimant was attending to his work, however, after the accident, he has stopped coming to the work.
In his cross-examination, he has stated that, he has not maintained any register of employment.
He also stated that he was giving salary to the employees only for the days on which they attended to their work and was not giving salary for the holidays.
He has identified the salary certificate at Ex.P-8 as issued by him.
Thus, in his cross- examination, though attempts were made to shaken the credibility of the evidence of PW-5, but the respondents could not able to do it completely and successfully.

Therefore, considering the evidence of PW-5 and his statement that for the holidays, the employees were not getting their salary, I am of the view that though the prevailing notional income for the relevant year 2011 was at `6,500/- per month, but there are all the evidence and material to take the income of the claimant in the instant case as at a sum of `8,000/- per month.
- 18

- Thus, when the income of the claimant is taken at a sum of `8,000/- per month, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of income during the treatment period which is at `10,000/-, without mentioning as to the duration/period during which the claimant has sustained the loss of income, requires a re- visit.

The Tribunal, by merely stating that the claimant must have taken rest and laid down for several months, has, without any calculation, awarded a lump sum of `10,000/- as compensation towards loss of earning during the treatment period.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case,
more particularly, the multiple grievous injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident, which are not less than seven fractures on different parts of his body including head and face
, I am of the view that, the claimant must have been advised and taken rest for at least a minimum period of five months.
Accordingly, towards loss of income for a period of five - 19 - months, he is entitled for compensation of a sum of `40,000/- (i.e. `8,000/-x5 months).
After deducting a sum of `10,000/- awarded by Tribunal, he is entitled for the differential amount of a sum of `30,000/- as enhancement under the said head.
19. The claimant has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident, he is suffering with permanent disability, as such, he could not continue his avocation.

In this regard,
he has got examined two Medical Doctors, i.e. PW-3 and PW-4 the Medico Legal Expert and a Ravichandra S vs Santhosh on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197754231/
8 Plastic Surgeon, who led their evidence and have assessed the disability of the claimant.

The sum and substance of their evidence though shows that the claimant was suffering with physical disability due to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident and assessed the permanent disability at 11% in his face, and with respect to the whole body at 10%, the Tribunal has accepted their assessment of percentage of disability to the whole body as at 10%.

Retaining the same - 20 - percentage of disability, for the age of the claimant, which is shown to be 28 years in the medical records, for which the multiplier applicable is '17', the quantum of compensation towards loss of future income would be at `1,63,200/- (i.e. `8,000/-x12x'17'x10/100).
After deducting a sum of `1,22,400/- awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is entitled for the differential amount of a sum of `40,800/- as enhancement under the said head.

20. It is considering the evidence of PW-3 and Ex.P-7 where the expected future medical expenses is said to be `25,000/-, the Tribunal has awarded `30,000/- under the said head, which is `5,000/-
more than the medical evidence, the same does not warrant any further enhancement.

21. It is after taking into consideration the evidence of the Medico Legal Expert and the Neuro Surgeon who were examined as PW-3 And PW-4 respectively and also considering the evidence of PW-1 and the nature of injuries sustained by him and the disfiguration of his body - 21 - including face, the Tribunal since has awarded a sum of `50,000/- as compensation towards loss of marriage prospects to the claimant, who claims himself to be an un- married person, I do not want to modify the said compensation any further, since the same is just and reasonable in the circumstances of the case.
22. Barring the above, the claimant is neither entitled for compensation under any other heads nor the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the existing heads deserves any further modification.
23. Thus, as analysed above, the claimant is entitled for a modified compensation as tabulated below:

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER [i] The appeal filed by the claimant stands allowed in part;

[ii] The impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate and Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal at Puttur, dated 01-06-2015, in M.V.C. No.1391/2012, is hereby modified to the extent that the compensation awarded at `5,02,400/- is enhanced by a sum of `1,00,800/- (Rupees One Lakh and Eight Hundred only), thus fixing the - 23 - total compensation at `6,03,200/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Three Thousand Two Hundred only).
[iii] The liability fixed by the Tribunal upon R-1 to R-3 jointly and severally and directing the Respondent No.3 Insurance Company to deposit the amount and also awarding rate of interest at `6% per annum on the awarded amount remains unaltered, as such, stands applicable to the enhanced sum also.
[iv] The enhanced amount with interest be deposited by the Respondent No.3 Insurance Company, before the Tribunal, within a period of six weeks from today.
[v] In view of the order of this Court dated 13-03-2018 passed on I.A.No.1/2017 in this appeal, the appellant/claimant is not entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation of a sum of `1,00,800/- for the delayed period of 472 days in filing the present appeal.

- Thus, when the income of the claimant is taken at a sum of `8,000/- per month, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of income during the treatment period which is at `10,000/-, without mentioning as to the duration/period during which the claimant has sustained the loss of income, requires a re- visit.
The Tribunal, by merely stating that the claimant must have taken rest and laid down for several months, has, without any calculation, awarded a lump sum of `10,000/- as compensation towards loss of earning during the treatment period.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case,
more particularly, the multiple grievous injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident, which are not less than seven fractures on different parts of his body including head and face
, I am of the view that, the claimant must have been advised and taken rest for at least a minimum period of five months.
Accordingly, towards loss of income for a period of five - 19 - months, he is entitled for compensation of a sum of `40,000/- (i.e. `8,000/-x5 months).
After deducting a sum of `10,000/- awarded by Tribunal, he is entitled for the differential amount of a sum of `30,000/- as enhancement under the said head.
The sum and substance of their evidence though shows that the claimant was suffering with physical disability due to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident and assessed the permanent disability at 11% in his face, and with respect to the whole body at 10%, the Tribunal has accepted their assessment of percentage of disability to the whole body as at 10%.
Retaining the same - 20 - percentage of disability, for the age of the claimant, which is shown to be 28 years in the medical records, for which the multiplier applicable is '17', the quantum of compensation towards loss of future income would be at `1,63,200/- (i.e. `8,000/-x12x'17'x10/100).
After deducting a sum of `1,22,400/- awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is entitled for the differential amount of a sum of `40,800/- as enhancement under the said head.
